articles.summary:
The latest EIA data showed that weekly U.S. crude oil production rose slightly in the week ending November 28 to 13.815 million bpd on average, 47,000 bpd under the all-time high.

Primary Vision’s Frac Spread Count, an estimate of the number of crews completing wells, fell in the week ending November 26, gaining 4 to reach 173. This is down from 201 at the beginning of the year. [...] ### Premium Content

# US Oil Rig Count Stages A Comeback After Last Week’s Losses

By Julianne Geiger - Dec 05, 2025, 12:19 PM CST

Powder river rig

The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States rose this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Friday, after last week’s sharp decline.

The total rig count in the US rose by 5 to 549 this week, according to Baker Hughes, down 40 from this same time last year. [...] The number of active drilling rigs in the Permian Basin stayed the same last week at 251 this week, which is 53 rigs under year-ago levels. The count in the Eagle Ford fell by 1, landing at 38, which is 10 fewer than this same time last year.

By 12:49 p.m. ET, the WTI benchmark was trading up on the day, gaining $0.59 to $60.26. The Brent benchmark was trading up $0.66 per barrel, at $63.92—up more than $1 week over week.

By Julianne Geiger for Oilprice.com

articles.summary: # Transocean (RIG) Up 5.2% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue? It has been about a month since the last earnings report for Transocean (RIG). Transocean reported second-quarter 2025 breakeven adjusted earnings per share in contrast to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of a loss of 1 cent. The bottom line also improved from the year-ago period’s reported loss of 15 cents. This improvement can be attributed to a strong second-quarter result from RIG's segments.s. This Switzerland-based offshore drilling powerhouse’s total adjusted revenues of $988 million beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $968 million. Ultra-deepwater and harsh environment revenues beat the consensus mark of $690 million and $257 million, respectively. Transocean’s ultra-deepwater floaters contributed 70.7% to net contract drilling revenues, while harsh environment floaters accounted for the remaining 29.3%. Revenues from the ultra-deepwater and harsh environment floaters totaled $699 million and $289 million, respectively, compared with the year-ago quarter’s reported figures of $606 million and $255 million. Revenues from ultra-deepwater operations were down from the model estimate of $703.5 million, while the same from harsh environment operations exceeded the prediction of $267.9 million. Average day rates in the reported quarter increased to $458,600 from $438,300 in the year-ago quarter. Average revenues per day from ultra-deepwater floaters increased to $457,200 from $433,900 in the year-ago quarter. The same from harsh environment floaters also increased to $462,400 from $449,600 in the prior-year quarter. The company reported $823 million in costs and expenses, which was 5.9% higher than the year-ago quarter’s level of $777 million. Additionally, operations and maintenance costs increased to $599 million from $534 million a year ago. The company reported its results for the quarter ended June 2025 more than a month ago. Nabors reported revenues of $832.79 million in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +13.3%. Nabors is expected to post a loss of $2.27 per share for the current quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +32.2%. Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -0.8%. articles.summary: # Transocean (RIG) Up 6.6% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Continue? A month has gone by since the last earnings report for Transocean (RIG). Revenues from the Ultra-deepwater and Harsh Environment floaters totaled $484 million and $165 million, respectively, compared with the year-ago quarter’s reported figures of $390 million and $196 million. Revenue efficiency was 97.8%, lower than 98.0% reported sequentially but higher than the year-ago quarter’s 94.9%. Average dayrates in the reported quarter increased to $364,100 from $334,500 in the year-ago quarter. Average revenues per day from Ultra-deepwater floaters increased to $360,000 from $305,600 in the year-ago quarter. Operations and maintenance (O&M) costs decreased to $409 million from $412 million a year ago. The company spent $81 million on capital investments in the first quarter. For the second quarter of 2023, Transocean expects adjusted contract drilling revenues of $735 million. For full-year 2023, the company expects operations and maintenance expenses of $1.9 billion. RIG expects net interest expenses for the second quarter in the range of $118-$479 million. Capital Expenditure (capex) is projected at $100 million, which includes $70 million related to new builds and $30 million for maintenance capex in the second quarter. Cash taxes are expected at about $15 million for the same quarter and roughly $35 million for full-year 2023. For the current quarter, Helmerich & Payne is expected to post earnings of $0.91 per share, indicating a change of +237% from the year-ago quarter. articles.summary: # The Biggest Crypto Events in the Last 30 Days: A Full Overview of Market Shifts, Technology, and Regulation. When analyzing the biggest crypto events of the last 30 days, it becomes clear that shifts in regulation, market movement, technological breakthroughs, and institutional behavior have reshaped the landscape. The market’s momentum over the past month has been a driving element in several of the biggest crypto events. With renewed interest from institutional players and stronger buying pressure across major digital assets, the overall sentiment has shifted from cautious optimism to a more confident, growth-oriented outlook. As is often the case, the largest asset dictated the direction of the entire ecosystem, making its recent surge one of the biggest crypto events of the month. Regulation has always played a major role in shaping digital asset markets, and in the last 30 days, it directly contributed to several of the biggest crypto events worldwide. Considering the pivotal role stablecoins play in global crypto transactions, this regulatory attention significantly influenced the past month’s developments. Technology-driven progress consistently shapes the biggest crypto events, and the last month was no exception. This merging of technologies has quickly become one of the biggest crypto events shaping the future direction of the industry. Crypto exchanges have remained central pillars of market activity, and several of their updates became major highlights among the biggest crypto events of the last 30 days. Many major platforms implemented security improvements, new multi-layer authentication procedures, and upgraded trading infrastructure. These enhancements increased investor confidence and reinforced the importance of exchange-level safety in a market that continues to attract new participants. Security remains a consistent theme in crypto, and several incidents in the last 30 days were significant enough to become part of the biggest crypto events of the period. ## What the Biggest Crypto Events Reveal About the Future. When reviewing the biggest crypto events of the last 30 days, one conclusion becomes unmistakably clear: the market is evolving into a more mature, structured environment. It is now shaped by coordinated infrastructure growth, global policy frameworks, and the increasing integration of blockchain with advanced technologies like AI.

articles.title: Analysis: Sliding US rig count outpaces efficiency gains, threatening onshore oil output
articles.summary:
"Now it is incremental and tweaking, whereas before it was a wholesale upgrade. Those things aren't going to make the level of efficiency gains we've seen in the last few years," Mosvold added.

Energy consultancies have similar estimates for the number of rigs needed to keep production steady in the Permian Basin, ranging between 240 and 260.

The Permian rig count last fell by one in the week to August 1, to 259, the lowest since September 2021, according to Baker Hughes. [...] "We have seen a 25% improvement over the last few years in rig efficiency, but the rig count has fallen over 30% over that same period. Put simply, the rig count declines have begun to outpace drilling efficiency gains," said Brandon Myers, head of research at Novi Labs.

"This is a recent development," he added. [...] In April 2019, the last time over 1,000 rigs were consistently deployed across the U.S., oil output stood at 12.14 million barrels per day (bpd). Today, there are just 540 rigs in operation, while output has jumped to some 13.5 million bpd.

Those close to the industry say that balance is fast approaching a tipping point, with analysts forecasting the rig count to fall further and U.S. onshore production to subsequently decline next year and into 2027.
